newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN GUNMAN ARRESTED AFTER WEEK ON THE RUN.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN GUNMAN ARRESTED AFTER WEEK ON THE RUN.

text.p: A fugitive gunman who eluded an intensive police and army manhunt in the forests of South Africa's northeast was arrested late on Monday after being on the run for over a week.

Former forester Mark Dewes, 40, was listed as most wanted man last week after he apparently snapped in a fit of rage and killed two people -- one of them the manager of a transport company he had been feuding with over the safety of their trucks.
He also wounded two people before fleeing into the heavily forested area, police said.

Police and soldiers launched a massive hunt for the man, who was armed with an automatic rifle and handguns, but he was arrested over 300 km (nearly 190 miles) away on Monday after his all-terrain vehicle was spotted west of Johannesburg.

"He was found in possession of a 9mm pistol, a big quantity of ammunition, a .357 magnum and an R1 (automatic) rifle with four magazines, which were loaded, as well as a (pocket) knife," police Captain Harry Shabangu told Reuters.
The shooting was sparked by an accident with one of the transport company's trucks. His ex-wife who was in his passenger seat smashed her head on the dashboard.
Dewes was apparently under stress, having been sacked by a forestry company earlier this year for allegedly assaulting a worker, a charge he denied.
He was also recently divorced, adding to the pressures on him, and was taking anti-depressants, family members said.
Dewes' brother who lives in the area where he was arrested, told reporters the fugitive had planned to turn himself in after his family had raised enough money for lawyers.
Until then, Dewes had said police could "forget it".
He was due to appear in an Mpumalanga provincial court within 48 hours of his arrest and would be kept in police cells until then, Shabangu said.
